stories.headline: Bihar floods worsen, several areas inundated as rivers continue rising
stories.title: Bihar floods worsen, several areas inundated as rivers continue rising
stories.summary: Patna, Sep 4 : The flood situation in Bihar deteriorated further on Friday as water levels of major rivers, including the Ganga, Gandak, Punpun and Dardha, continued to rise, inundating new areas across the state. According to the Water Resources Department, the Ganga is expected to cross its Highest Flood Level (HFL) at Patna's Gandhi Ghat and Hathidah in Mokama by Friday night. The state Disaster Management Department has issued an alert for residents living along riverbanks and in low-lying areas of Bhojpur, Patna, Saran, Vaishali, Nalanda, Begusarai, Lakhisarai and Jehanabad, urging them to remain vigilant and take precautionary measures. In Patna, the Ganga was flowing 1.17 metres above the danger mark at Digha, 1.67 metres above the danger mark at Gandhi Ghat and 1.32 metres above the danger mark at Hathidah. The Punpun River was recorded at 2.29 metres above the danger mark at Shripalpur, while the Dardha River was flowing 3.07 metres above the danger mark at Kolhachak. In Bhagalpur, the Ganga rose by 15 cm over the past 24 hours, leading to the re-entry of floodwaters into diara areas of Nathnagar, Naugachia and Pirpainti. Vast tracts of agricultural land, along with standing crops and fodder, have been submerged. Khagaria remains among the worst-hit districts, with the Ganga flowing 1.01 metres above the danger mark. The Kosi, Bagmati and Burhi Gandak rivers were also flowing significantly above danger levels, heightening concerns of further flooding. In Raghopur, severe erosion and land subsidence have been reported along a railway line after the near-complete erosion of a marginal embankment. The main channel of the Ganga has shifted dangerously close to the tracks, affecting areas within a two-to-three-kilometre radius. The Ganga's water level in Munger rose by 36 cm in the last 24 hours. In Madhepura district's Alamnagar and Chausa blocks, nearly one lakh people have been affected by floods, prompting authorities to deploy 35 boats for rescue and relief operations. In Banka district, a diversion road built for an under-construction bridge near Barsanda village was washed away by the strong current of the Mirchni River. Several villages in Saharsa have also been inundated. Floodwaters have disrupted road connectivity in several districts. In West Champaran, traffic has come to a standstill on the Yogapatti-Chhota Chaumukha-Siswa Mangalpur road, where water is flowing two to three feet above the roadway. Around two dozen villages in Samastipur have been affected by flooding, while several rural roads are submerged. Traffic movement has also been disrupted on the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge in Patna. All panchayats in Raghopur block of Vaishali district have been affected, with nearly 20 panchayats losing road connectivity to the main network, hampering relief operations and the movement of residents. --IANS

stories.headline: India offers DNA profiling facilities to identify Nepal flood victims
stories.title: India offers DNA profiling facilities to identify Nepal flood victims
stories.summary: India will make central and state forensic laboratory facilities available for DNA profiling of the close biological relatives of people missing in Nepal’s devastating flash floods, the Ministry of External Affairs said.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: India will make central and state forensic laboratory facilities available for DNA profiling of the close biological relatives of people missing in Nepal’s devastating flash floods, the Ministry of External Affairs said.
The measure is intended to assist Nepalese authorities in identifying bodies recovered after the 26 August disaster, which has killed at least 1,259 people.
Nearly 5,000 people remain missing, while emergency teams have rescued more than 12,000.

First-degree biological relatives living in India — including a missing person’s father, mother, son, daughter or sibling — may have their samples collected and DNA profiles prepared at designated laboratories.

These include Central Forensic Science Laboratories, State Forensic Science Laboratories, laboratories operated by the National Forensic Sciences University and facilities accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories that are equipped to conduct DNA profiling.
The decision was taken by the Union Ministry of Home Affairs as an additional step to support the identification process under way in Nepal.
It followed a statement issued by the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu outlining the procedures available for identifying the mortal remains of flood victims.

“As advised by the Nepal Police, Autosomal STR DNA profiling may be undertaken for the purpose of identification, subject to the technical requirements communicated by the Nepali authorities,” the MEA said.
Autosomal short tandem repeat profiling is commonly used to establish biological relationships and assist in the identification of human remains.
Once prepared, the DNA profiles and preliminary information sought by Nepalese authorities may be emailed to dnacodis@nepalpolice.gov.np for comparison with DNA obtained from unidentified bodies.
Families may also send a copy of the DNA profile to eoikathmandufloodsupport@gmail.com to enable the Indian Embassy in Kathmandu to assist with coordination.
The helpline number for the process is +977 9841 6160 95.

stories.headline: Daily weather tracker: Heavy rainfall expected across more than 20 states; flash flood threat looms over Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh & Rajasthan
stories.title: Daily weather tracker: Heavy rainfall expected across more than 20 states; flash flood threat looms over Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh & Rajasthan
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Heavy rainfall threatens over 20 states, with Madhya Pradesh facing very heavy showers and heightened flash flood risks in vulnerable districts.
Uttar Pradesh and eastern Rajasthan brace for intense rainfall, sudden flooding, waterlogging and dangerous rises in rivers and local streams.
Bihar, Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and northeastern states expect heavy rain, thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds through Friday.
Southern India faces thunderstorms and lightning, with winds reaching 40 to 50 kilometres per hour in several affected regions.
Palayamkottai records 40.2 degrees Celsius, while Cherrapunji receives 70 millimetres rainfall amid widespread monsoon activity across the country.

Large parts of India remained under the grip of an active monsoon on Friday, September 4, as very heavy rainfall threatened more than 20 states and raised concerns over flash floods, waterlogging, thunderstorms and strong winds.

According to the latest weather update issued by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Friday morning, a low-pressure area over northern Madhya Pradesh and adjoining southern Uttar Pradesh is expected to remain nearly stationary for the next two days.
The system is likely to trigger widespread rain accompanied by thunderstorms and gusty winds across Madhya Pradesh and neighbouring regions.

The monsoon trough continues to remain active, extending from Bikaner and Sikar in Rajasthan through northern Madhya Pradesh and adjoining southern Uttar Pradesh, before moving towards Daltonganj in Jharkhand, Berhampore in West Bengal and onward to Tripura.
Madhya Pradesh is expected to be among the worst-affected states on Friday, with an orange alert issued for heavy to very heavy rainfall.
Rainfall between 115.6 mm to 204.4 mm is possible in isolated areas.
The northern and western districts face an increased risk of waterlogging and sudden flooding, particularly in low-lying areas and near rivers and streams.

stories.headline: Gaurav Gogoi Urges ECI to Intervene in Nagaon Lok Sabha Bye-Election
stories.title: Gaurav Gogoi Urges ECI to Intervene in Nagaon Lok Sabha Bye-Election
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: Today, Congress MP from Jorhat Gaurav Gogoi has urged the Election Commission of India (ECI) to urgently intervene in the upcoming Nagaon Lok Sabha bye-election, raising concerns over the resignation of Nagaon District Commissioner Debasish Sharma.

In a social media post on Twitter, Gogoi alleged that Sharma, while serving as DC-cum-District Election Officer (DEO), had overseen several sensitive aspects of the electoral process in recent months.
He claimed that decisions taken during Sharma’s tenure could have implications for the neutrality and fairness of the forthcoming bye-election.
Gogoi called on the ECI to order an independent, time-bound inquiry into Sharma’s tenure as DC-cum-DEO.
The Congress leader also urged the poll panel to take necessary steps to ensure a level playing field for all candidates and maintain public confidence in the electoral process.
Gogoi warned that any failure by the ECI to act on the concerns could undermine public trust in the conduct and credibility of the bye-election.

stories.headline: Adani Ports’ rising volumes, overseas push to keep growth story intact
stories.title: Adani Ports’ rising volumes, overseas push to keep growth story intact
stories.summary: Growth may pick up further in the seasonally strong second half, given the relatively healthy volumes despite disruptions caused by the West Asia war.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd’s business update for August reflects strong momentum with cargo handled across its ports growing by 19% year-on-year to 50 million tonnes (mt).
With this, growth in the first two months of the September quarter (Q2FY27) now exceeds 18%, up from 14.5% in Q1FY27.
Given the relatively healthy volumes despite the disruption caused by the West Asia war, growth may pick up further in the seasonally strong second half.
However, these numbers include the North Queensland Export Terminal (NQXT) in Australia, which Adani Ports acquired in December.

“Assuming a quarterly run rate of 10-11mt for NQXT, as seen in the past, volumes for August (excluding NQXT) work out to 46mt, up about 10.5% on-year (versus 7% on-year estimated for July), potentially indicating improvement in underlying volume growth,” noted JM Financial Institutional Securities.
Q1FY27 volumes, excluding NQXT, had grown by 6.2%.

So, for the first five months of FY27, total volumes handled have grown by 16% to 234mt, a tad higher than the required15% compound annual growth rate over FY26-31, to reach its target of 1 billion tonnes of cargo handling by FY31.
However, logistics remain a weak spot, with rail container volumes declining by about 11% in Q2FY27 to date, following a 19% decline in Q1.
The company could well be pivoting towards more profitable segments as the share of logistics in Ebitda was only 3.3% in Q1 despite an 11% revenue contribution.
Ebitda is short for earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.
Notably, Q1FY27 financials were strong.
Consolidated Ebitda rose by 19% on-year to ₹6,540 crore.

stories.headline: Trump turns to dual economic, military approach in latest attempt to squeeze Iran
stories.title: Trump turns to dual economic, military approach in latest attempt to squeeze Iran
stories.summary: Washington, Sep 04: Confronted by an intransigent Iranian government that has refused to back down in the face of a massive military campaign, President Donald Trump appears to have settled on a dual-pronged approach that combines economic pressure with the potential of a devastating escalation in force. Having launched “Operation Economic Outcast” just last week to try to isolate Iran from its remaining global trade partners, the Trump administration also resumed strikes in recent days, prompting Iranian retaliation that has renewed concerns of an all-out regional war. However, the combination of already intense sanctions on Iran and an off-and-on bombing campaign since the war began more than six months ago has not bowed the Iranian leadership and has left the administration struggling to find a way to wind down the conflict. Tehran has dug in its heels -- to Trump's frustration -- as energy prices rise, the global economy roils and poll numbers on the administration's handling of the war dip ahead of November's midterm congressional elections. Trump said Wednesday that he didn't think the conflict would last “much longer,” but he again shrugged off suggestions that its unpopularity and high gasoline prices resulting from Iran's chokehold on the Strait of Hormuz would affect the elections for Republicans. “It doesn't matter. And I'm not affected by the election,” he told reporters. "I'm not running. But my party is running, and I'm going to help my party. But I think my party respects the fact that we're not allowing Iran to have a nuclear weapon.” A regional diplomat briefed on the matter described the current impasse between Tehran and Washington as reflective of both countries' domestic priorities: the midterm elections for Trump and Republicans and the internal crises within Iran. Domestic issues are critical reasons why neither side is willing to blink first, said the diplomat, who spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive negotiations. The diplomat said negotiations, including those between Iran and Oman or even Iran and the US, will not go anywhere without addressing the initial catalyst of war: Israel. And the diplomat was sceptical of the Trump administration's new sanctions plan, saying the threats require more explanation than what the US has provided so far. The Trump administration's economic isolation of Iran is off to a slow start The administration's new push for Iran's economic isolation was announced with great fanfare last week and a dire warning for all remaining countries to cut off financial and trade ties with Iran or face US retaliation -- but the campaign so far has fallen flat. Just one branch of an Egyptian bank in the United Arab Emirates has been targeted so far. For actual sanctions to bite, experts agree that they must apply to Iran's main trading partners: mainly China but also India and Russia. But Trump is loath to target China, especially as he is preparing to host President Xi Jinping later this month. Trump also insists that the US has control over the Strait of Hormuz, where one-fifth of the world's oil transits before the war began. The strategic waterway has been a key pressure point for Iran, and reopening it fully has become one of the prime goals for the US administration. Ship traffic through the strait is well below pre-war levels due to the risk of attack if vessels don't comply with an Iranian vetting regime near its coastline, which is in sharp contrast to the unhindered navigation before the war. There were 102 transits last week and 126 the week before, according to shipping data company Lloyd's List Intelligence, compared with 130 or more per day before the war. “As President Trump said, the strait is open, and all mines have been cleared,” White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said Thursday. “The naval blockade remains in full force and effect, and Operation Economic Outcast is underway to sever every remaining economic lifeline sustaining the regime.” The White House has repeatedly touted the economic impact that the sanctions have had on Iran, citing its rampant inflation and the massive loss in the value of its currency. US officials have described Iran's financial system as “one big house of cards.” Going forward, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said “the price” Iran will pay will be primarily economic, “but we reserve the right ... to take military action when necessary -- not just to protect ourselves but to prevent them from being able to threaten others as well.” “They're going to continue to feel the squeeze,” he told Fox News host Brian Kilmeade in an interview that aired Wednesday. Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that he would not characterise the current situation as a “war” but that the administration would respond to any Iranian hostile action. “Major combat operations are currently not ongoing, and they haven't been ongoing in a very long time," Vance told reporters during a White House briefing. "In fact, what we did just a couple of days ago is that we made it harder for the Iranians to shoot at commercial shipping again in order to ensure the flow of oil and gas into world energy markets.” Combining military force and sanctions on Iran is the only option,' one analyst says Complicating things for the US, Iran's leadership has shown signs of divisions between moderates more open to a diplomatic solution and hardliners who want to press ahead with a more confrontational approach. President Masoud Pezeshkian is one of the most prominent voices still calling for a negotiated solution. But the hardliners appear to have gained the upper hand, and Iran shows no sign of backing down. Tehran continues to lash out at US interests and allies around the region in response to military strikes. “This kind of a hybrid approach -- the combination of military force, blockade and economic pressure -- is the only option that seems to be available to the United States at this moment,” said Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst for the International Crisis Group. Still, he said, “it's been for a long time, but now maybe more than ever, a battle of endurance between the two sides.” Amr Hamzawy, director of the Middle East program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, pointed to two main reasons for the deteriorating situation. “One, none of the two parties is satisfied with the outcome -- meaning that the current situation does not serve US interests well, and it does not serve Iranian interests well,” Hamzawy said. The other reason is how leaders from both sides are perceived at home. “The Trump administration is afraid of being portrayed in the US as an administration that failed to end a military campaign successfully, and that's going to impact the midterm elections," he said. “And the Iranians, especially the Revolutionary Guard, are quite afraid of appearing as if they are submitting to US sanctions with no actions on their side, which might hurt them domestically.”

Just one branch of an Egyptian bank in the United Arab Emirates has been targeted so far.
For actual sanctions to bite, experts agree that they must apply to Iran's main trading partners: mainly China but also India and Russia.
But Trump is loath to target China, especially as he is preparing to host President Xi Jinping later this month.
Trump also insists that the US has control over the Strait of Hormuz, where one-fifth of the world's oil transits before the war began.
The strategic waterway has been a key pressure point for Iran, and reopening it fully has become one of the prime goals for the US administration.

Ship traffic through the strait is well below pre-war levels due to the risk of attack if vessels don't comply with an Iranian vetting regime near its coastline, which is in sharp contrast to the unhindered navigation before the war.
There were 102 transits last week and 126 the week before, according to shipping data company Lloyd's List Intelligence, compared with 130 or more per day before the war.
“As President Trump said, the strait is open, and all mines have been cleared,” White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said Thursday.

“The naval blockade remains in full force and effect, and Operation Economic Outcast is underway to sever every remaining economic lifeline sustaining the regime.” The White House has repeatedly touted the economic impact that the sanctions have had on Iran, citing its rampant inflation and the massive loss in the value of its currency.

US officials have described Iran's financial system as “one big house of cards.” Going forward, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said “the price” Iran will pay will be primarily economic, “but we reserve the right...

to take military action when necessary -- not just to protect ourselves but to prevent them from being able to threaten others as well.” “They're going to continue to feel the squeeze,” he told Fox News host Brian Kilmeade in an interview that aired Wednesday.
Vice President JD Vance said Thursday that he would not characterise the current situation as a “war” but that the administration would respond to any Iranian hostile action.
“Major combat operations are currently not ongoing, and they haven't been ongoing in a very long time," Vance told reporters during a White House briefing.

"In fact, what we did just a couple of days ago is that we made it harder for the Iranians to shoot at commercial shipping again in order to ensure the flow of oil and gas into world energy markets.” Combining military force and sanctions on Iran is the only option,' one analyst says Complicating things for the US, Iran's leadership has shown signs of divisions between moderates more open to a diplomatic solution and hardliners who want to press ahead with a more confrontational approach.
President Masoud Pezeshkian is one of the most prominent voices still calling for a negotiated solution.
But the hardliners appear to have gained the upper hand, and Iran shows no sign of backing down.

“This kind of a hybrid approach -- the combination of military force, blockade and economic pressure -- is the only option that seems to be available to the United States at this moment,” said Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst for the International Crisis Group.

Still, he said, “it's been for a long time, but now maybe more than ever, a battle of endurance between the two sides.” Amr Hamzawy, director of the Middle East program at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, pointed to two main reasons for the deteriorating situation.
“One, none of the two parties is satisfied with the outcome -- meaning that the current situation does not serve US interests well, and it does not serve Iranian interests well,” Hamzawy said.
The other reason is how leaders from both sides are perceived at home.
“The Trump administration is afraid of being portrayed in the US as an administration that failed to end a military campaign successfully, and that's going to impact the midterm elections," he said.
“And the Iranians, especially the Revolutionary Guard, are quite afraid of appearing as if they are submitting to US sanctions with no actions on their side, which might hurt them domestically.”

stories.headline: Molvi Imran Ansari Meets Iranian Chief Justice Ayatollah Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje’i in New Delhi
stories.title: Molvi Imran Ansari Meets Iranian Chief Justice Ayatollah Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje’i in New Delhi
stories.summary: New Delhi, September 3 : President of the All Jammu and Kashmir Shia Association (AJKSA) and JKPC General Secretary, Molvi Imran Ansari on Thursda met the Chief Justice of the Islamic Republic of Iran, Ayatollah Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje’i, during his official visit to New Delhi for the BRICS judicial leaders’ summit. The meeting was also attended by Dr. Mohammad Fathali, Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to India, and Dr. Abdul Majid Hakeem Ilahi, Representative of the Supreme Leader of Iran in India. During the interaction, Molvi Imran Ansari conveyed his respect for the people of Iran and remembered the martyrs of Iran, including Ayatollah Sayyid Ali Hosseini Khamenei, as well as the innocent victims of the tragic Minab school incident, particularly the children. He offered prayers for the departed and expressed solidarity with their families. Speaking about Kashmir’s historic relationship with Iran, Molvi Imran Ansari said that the connection between the two societies goes back centuries and is deeply rooted in civilization rather than politics alone. Persian language and literature, Islamic scholarship, poetry, architecture, art and traditional crafts have all played an important role in shaping Kashmir’s cultural and intellectual heritage. For generations, scholars and ideas travelled between these regions, creating a relationship of faith, knowledge and mutual respect. Imran Ansari also spoke about the historic relationship between India and Iran, describing the two countries as ancient civilizations connected through centuries of cultural exchange, trade and people-to-people relations. He said that these historic ties remain a strong foundation for an even more meaningful partnership in the modern era. He expressed hope that the renewed engagement between India and Iran would open a new chapter in bilateral relations, particularly in the fields of trade, connectivity, education, culture, science, technology and regional cooperation. He noted that the strengthening of contemporary relations between the two nations carries the potential to build upon their glorious shared past and create new opportunities for future generations. Molvi Imran Ansari further emphasized the importance of unity, education, compassion and peaceful dialogue in the present times. Referring to the teachings of Karbala, he said that its message of faith, courage, justice, patience and moral strength continues to guide humanity. The meeting reflected the longstanding bonds of respect and shared heritage between Kashmir and Iran and reaffirmed the importance of strengthening the historic friendship and growing partnership between India and the Islamic Republic of Iran.

stories.title: Karnataka Cabinet clears sites for BMIC-affected farmers under Supreme Court pressure
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
article_sentences: Following directions from the Supreme Court, the Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday, September 4, approved the allotment of sites to 1,453 farmers who lost their land to the Bangalore-Mysore Infrastructure Corridor project (BMIC).

Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara said farmers who had lost less than one acre of land would be compensated with a 1,200 sq ft plot, while those who lost more than an acre would be given a 2,400 sq ft plot.
"Though this is not part of the Framework Agreement signed, the Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprise has agreed to compensate.
It has already developed 574 plots, and the rest need to be approved.
Four places have been identified for the same.
The plots will be given in two months," he said.
The Cabinet's decision comes days after the Karnataka High Court delivered a scathing judgement on the poor implementation of the BMIC project by the Nandi Infrastructure Corridor Enterprise (NICE).

Although Janata Dal (Secular) leader HD Kumaraswamy kept taking the government to task, the political response was largely centred on the toll collected by NICE allegedly illegally, while there was near complete silence on the company's utter failure to deliver on the project nearly 30 years after it was formalised.

There is practically no outrage over the fact that a private company acquired thousands of acres of land for the project but built practically nothing and instead sold off portions of the land to private players in violation of its legal obligations.
Dozens of landowners, who had gone unpaid for more than 20 years after their land was acquired for the project, had approached the High Court seeking to have the acquisition quashed.
In 2025, a single-judge bench of the High Court ruled in favour of the landowners and quashed the acquisition; a division bench upheld that order on July 29.

"The facts as disclosed would clearly suggest that there is nothing nice about the NICE project except that the farmers have been robbed of their lands and livelihood of generations without payment of compensation," the High Court said while upholding the landowners' claims.

stories.title: Tata Motors gets Italy market regulator nod for Iveco takeover offer
stories.summary: Tata Motors to pay €14.10 per common share of Iveco Group, including dividend, to shareholders; acceptance period opens September 7
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: Tata Motors on Friday said Italy's market regulator Consob has approved the offer document for its voluntary tender offer to acquire all common shares of Iveco Group NV.
The acceptance period for Iveco shareholders will begin on September 7 and close on October 26, unless extended, Tata Motors said in a regulatory filing.
Under the offer, Tata Motors will pay €14.10 per common share of Iveco Group, including dividend, to shareholders.
TML CV Holdings BV, an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors, received Consob's approval for the offer document on September 3, 2026.
Shareholders who tender their shares during the acceptance period will be paid on October 30, 2026, unless the offer period is extended.
If legal conditions are met, the acceptance period will reopen for five trading days, from November 2 to November 6, with payment scheduled for November 13, 2026.

The offer document, which contains the detailed terms of the offer and procedures for accepting it, will be published and disseminated through modalities to be specified in a subsequent press release, the company said.
The offer will open in Italy and be extended to shareholders in the United States in accordance with relevant securities regulations.
The filing said the acceptance period has not started yet and that the press release is for information purposes only and does not constitute an offer to buy, or a solicitation to sell, securities.
Tata Motors had announced its decision to promote the offer through TML CV Holdings Pte Ltd in July 2025.

stories.title: Andhra Pradesh Cabinet clears reclassification of 22.31 acres in Nellore for house sites
stories.summary: The decision was taken on the recommendations of a joint committee, with specific safeguards to protect the functioning and maintenance of the Sarvepalli canal
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet clears' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Andhra Pradesh Cabinet on Thursday (September 3, 2026), chaired by Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, approved a proposal to reclassify 22.31 acres of land in Nellore Urban mandal of SPSR Nellore district from ‘canal poramboke’ to ‘A.W. dry’ and issue house-site pattas to eligible poor beneficiaries in the area.
The decision was taken on the recommendations of a joint committee, with specific safeguards to protect the functioning and maintenance of the Sarvepalli canal.
Of the total 62.70 acres under consideration, the reclassification will exclude the active canal area, the hydraulic operational zone and the mandatory 20-foot irrigation right-of-way buffer.

According to the Cabinet decision, the land classification change will be permitted only in areas that do not interfere with the canal’s water-carrying capacity or the Irrigation Department’s maintenance rights.
The protected zones will continue to remain available for canal operations and maintenance.
The government has also authorised the issuance of house-site pattas to eligible economically weaker beneficiaries on the reclassified land.
Officials have been directed to ensure that the prescribed safeguards are maintained while implementing the decision.
The approval is aimed at making suitable land available for housing for poor families while safeguarding the canal infrastructure, water flow and the Irrigation Department’s operational requirements.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Expresses Shock At 8 Year Custody Of Undertrial, Denies Bail Citing Antecedents; Fast-Tracks Trial
stories.title: Supreme Court Expresses Shock At 8 Year Custody Of Undertrial, Denies Bail Citing Antecedents; Fast-Tracks Trial
stories.summary: The Court expressed concern at the slow-progress of trial.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Court expressed concern at the slow-progress of trial.

The Supreme Court on Tuesday (01.09.2026) has declined to grant bail to an undertrial prisoner who has been in judicial custody for over eight-and-a-half years in a burglary case, holding that his antecedents involving offences of a similar nature to the present case weighed against exercise of the Court's discretion.
However, taking note of the prolonged incarceration and the slow pace of trial, the Court directed the trial court to complete the entire trial within six months.
The appellant, alongwith the other accused persons, was traced by the Anti-Dacoity Section of the Detective Department, Kolkata.
Police.
The case relates to burglary inside a jewellery shop, in commission of which the accused persons assaulted the shop owner and his employees to take all the jewelleries kept in the display boxes.
It is alleged that 752.100 grams (then amounting to Rs 21,66,048) of gold jewelleries were taken away in the said act.
Appellant's bail plea was rejected by the Calcutta High Court, subsequent to which he approached the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court expressed concern over the extraordinarily long period the petitioner has spent behind bars without trial being concluded.

It recorded that the petitioner has been in judicial custody as an undertrial accused for the past eight years and six months, and that till date, only six witnesses have been examined, calling the situation “shocking”.

Despite the prolonged custody, the Court declined to grant bail, noting that it would have considered the plea favourably solely on the ground of the long period undergone as an undertrial, but for the petitioner's antecedents.
The bench ruled so considering the petitioner's prior involvements in offences of the very same nature as those with which he has been charged in the present case.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Thursday issued notice on an MBBS student's plea seeking direction asking Chettinad Academy of Research and Education to grant her course completion certificate and MBBS Degree Certificate without insisting on repayment of the fee which was seized by the NIA for alleged terror links.
A bench of Justice Vikram Nath and Justice Sandeep Mehta will hear the matter on 13th October.

The SLP has been filed by a student named Puja Kumari, against the order of a division bench of the Madras High Court, which upheld a Single Judge order refusing to direct the college and medical council authorities to release her course completion certificate and MBBS degree.
The fee paid by the student during her MBBS course was seized by the National Investigation Agency (NIA), on the ground that the fee was funded through Maoist activities.
During the student's tenure, Rs 1,13,70,500/- was periodically remitted to her account.

Later, during the course of a criminal investigation, the NIA alleged that the funds utilized to pay the student's fee were directly derived from illegal, extorted funds raised on behalf of the Communist Party of India (Maoist), a proscribed terrorist organization.
The NIA seized the funds after notice to the college.
The college then withheld the student's documents over non-realisation of legitimate institutional fee.
The student argued that educational certificates could not be retained as security or treated like financial deposits under general lien.

She also denied any personal involvement or connection with any unlawful or terrorist organisation and pointed out that she had a clean, impeccable record and had cleared her medical curriculum without any blemish.

The Madras High Court Division Bench rejected her appeal seeking course completion, observing that if the student was in fact innocent, she could approach the Special NIA Court for releasing the seized funds.
The court added that the college could not be expected to litigate against the NIA to retrieve the fee.

stories.headline: RAKSHA: India’s 10-year blueprint for defence diplomacy and global strategic partnerships
stories.title: RAKSHA: India’s 10-year blueprint for defence diplomacy and global strategic partnerships
stories.summary: The strategic blueprint seeks to integrate defence diplomacy more closely with India’s wider foreign policy, economic interests and national security objectives
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'national security' in summary weight 42
article_sentences: India unveiled an ambitious new framework to guide its defence diplomacy over the next decade, signalling a more structured and proactive approach towards building strategic partnerships across the world.

The document, titled ‘RAKSHA’, lays down a comprehensive roadmap for strengthening India’s military engagement, defence industrial cooperation and global security partnerships in line with its long-term national interests.

Released by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in New Delhi on Thursday (September 3, 2026), the strategic blueprint seeks to integrate defence diplomacy more closely with India’s wider foreign policy, economic interests and national security objectives.

At a time of growing geopolitical competition, regional conflicts and rapidly changing military technologies, the framework underlines New Delhi’s effort to emerge as a more influential and dependable security partner.
A senior Defence official informed that the central idea behind RAKSHA is that defence diplomacy can no longer remain limited to ceremonial military exchanges, high-level visits and joint exercises.

Instead, India is seeking to build long-term, outcome-oriented partnerships that contribute to regional stability, strengthen military capabilities, expand industrial cooperation and promote Indian defence products in global markets.
One of the key pillars of the framework is the deepening of strategic partnerships.
India has significantly expanded its defence engagement in recent years with countries across the Indo-Pacific, Europe, West Asia, Africa and other regions.
RAKSHA provides a broader direction for these engagements by identifying areas where India’s strategic interests and those of partner countries converge.
Recently, India signed an agreement with Indonesia to deliver BrahMos supersonic cruise missile system and Astra Mk-1 beyond the visual-range air-to-air missiles.
The blueprint also places strong emphasis on capacity building and military cooperation.
Training programmes for foreign military personnel have traditionally been an important component of India’s defence diplomacy.

article_sentences: New Delhi: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday congratulated Belgium for co-hosting the recently concluded Hockey World Cup 2026, while also praising the Indian men’s and women’s teams for their outings in the global showpiece.

PM Modi addressed the media after his meeting with Belgium PM Bart De Wever in New Delhi, as he praised Belgium and the Netherlands for hosting the tournament, where Germany won the men’s title, while Argentina clinched the women’s crown.
“Belgium and the Netherlands hosted the Hockey World Cup last month.
